subject: Fill specific countries with different colour

messages.author: 28ae80d044e80756
messages.subject: Fill specific countries with different colour
parts:
Hey guys,

I made a map with rworldmap and right now my code looks like this:

library(rworldmap)

newmap <- getMap(resolution = "high")
plot(newmap, xlim = c(-10,19), ylim c(40,56), col = "gray90", fill = TRUE)

This gives me a certain excerpt of Europe with all countries colored in light gray. Now, I would like to additionally highlight Spain, France, Belgium, Germany, Italy, Austria and Czech Republic (preferably in darker gray) but I absolutely don´t know how to do it. I tried several things I found on the internet but it did not work...

I hope there is an easy way to do it ;-)

Many thanks in advance!

messages.author: 81b6b3d7dfea88a5
messages.subject: Re: [rworldmap group] Fill specific countries with different colour
parts:
Hi Sarah,

You're nearly there. This in reply to a later message you sent me. You were missing a c in the first line, and Name needed to be NAME. Then this should be all you need to start with a 2 grey map.

dF <- data.frame(country = c("spain","france","belgium","germany","austria","italy"), sampled = c(1,1,1,2,2,2))
sPDF <- joinCountryData2Map(dF,joinCode = "NAME", nameJoinColumn = "country", mapResolution = "low")
mapCountryData(sPDF, nameColumnToPlot= "sampled", catMethod = 'categorical', xlim=c(-10,19), ylim=c(40,56), colourPalette=c("gray90","gray30"))

Add extra countries and you can change sampled to e.g. sampled = c("name1","name1","name1","name2","name2","name2")

Help creating a map of Europe is the least I can do on a sad day like today !

Might also be worth looking at the tmap package which is good for doing this type of thing too and a bit newer.

Good luck,
Andy

Hi Sarah,
The default map is in lat long. It is possible to re-project the map using rgdal, but to be honest I'd reccommend having a look at tmap which does projections and Europe maps better :

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/tmap/vignettes/tmap-nutshell.html

Enjoy your weekend too.
Andy
